scope: Invoicing gate chain (Delivered -> pallet sheets -> gate -> mark invoiced -> 043 guard), owner override, undo, pallet ledger 3-step confirm, pallet feeders and their callers, /pallets/* Worker routes, pl_* schema.

nodes.label: renderInvoicing

nodes.label: _invLoadGate

nodes.label: _invPESheetsOK

nodes.label: _invHasPrice

nodes.label: _invMarkInvoiced
nodes.notes: checks _invPESheetsOK then _invHasPrice then invoice number, then calls _invWriteInvoice.

nodes.label: _invWriteInvoice

nodes.label: _invUndoInvoice

nodes.label: _invOverrideInvoice

nodes.label: renderPalletLedger

nodes.label: _plvBlockReadOnly

nodes.label: plvDoConfirm
nodes.notes: 3 sequential HTTP calls: POST /pallets/sheets -> PATCH /pallets/movements/:id -> POST /pallets/movements/:id/confirm. No transaction across them (see FM-c-03).

nodes.label: plvPanelReverse

nodes.label: plvDoFix

nodes.label: openPalletUpload

Writes 'Pallet Sheet 1/2 Uploaded' (pallet_upload.js:573-580) and to legacy pallet_ledger_suppliers/partners — neither is read by the live gate (pl_v_order_gate). nodes.label: _checkPalletSheets

nodes.label: plFetch
nodes.notes: shared HTTP helper for every /pallets/* call (invoicing.js, pallet_ledger.js, pallet-feed.js itself). On !res.ok throws Error(data.error || 'HTTP '+res.status) — a 401 (expired JWT) surfaces as whatever jsonError('Unauthorized',401,...) put in data.error, generic and not a re-login prompt (cross_dep ε).

nodes.label: _plSafe
nodes.notes: every feeder wraps in this: catches all errors, shows a toast for 8s, RETURNS NULL — never blocks the order save/delete/assign that triggered it. If the toast is missed, the pallet movement is simply never created (FM-c-04).

nodes.label: plOnOrderSaved
nodes.notes: idempotent by order_stop_rec; creates/updates pending LOADING per Loading stop; deletes orphaned pending LOADING whose stop was removed (lines 87-94).

nodes.label: plOnDelivered
nodes.notes: auto-confirmed DELIVERY, net 0 (taken=given=stop pallets), body.confirm:true — no sheet required (Worker needsSheet=false for DELIVERY).

nodes.label: plOnIntlPartnerAssigned
nodes.notes: VS partner hand-over pending PARTNER_PICKUP/DROPOFF; refuses to touch a movement once confirmed (line 148) so a second order save never overwrites the ramp's final entry.

nodes.label: plOnExchangeOff / plOnOrderDeleted
nodes.notes: deletes ONLY pending movements of the order; confirmed stay as history. plOnOrderDeleted (190-192) is a bare alias calling this.

nodes.label: syncOrderDownstream
nodes.notes: team α owned cascade; calls plOnOrderSaved only when changedFields includes 'Pallet Exchange' (core/order-sync.js:96-101) — a SECOND, narrower trigger path than the unconditional call in submitIntlOrder/submitNatlOrder (cross_dep α).

nodes.label: submitIntlOrder
nodes.notes: calls plOnOrderSaved(savedOrderId,'intl') unconditionally on every save (line 2073), independent of syncOrderDownstream's conditional call.

nodes.label: deleteIntlOrder
nodes.notes: calls plOnOrderDeleted(recId,'intl') at line 3026, after RAMP cleanup, before ORDER_STOPS delete.

nodes.label: submitNatlOrder
nodes.notes: calls plOnOrderSaved(savedNatlId,'natl') at line 1443, inside a try/catch around ORDER_STOPS save (so a stops-save failure can skip the feeder call silently — swallowed by the outer catch, 1443-1444).

nodes.label: deleteNatlOrder
nodes.notes: calls plOnOrderDeleted(recId,'natl') at line 1953.

nodes.label: _opsDelFinal / _opsOvActFinal
nodes.notes: both delivery-confirm paths call plOnDelivered(id) WITHOUT await (line 936, 1103) — fire-and-forget; _plSafe absorbs errors so no unhandled rejection, but the caller never learns whether the pallet DELIVERY row was actually written before moving on.

nodes.label: _wiSaveFromPopover / _wiClear

failure_modes.what: When /pallets/gate fails (INV.gateFailed=true), the fallback per-stop check reads 'Pallet Sheet 1/2 Uploaded' — fields that nothing in the live app writes any more since the pallet_upload.js entry point was removed 7/9/2026 (orders_intl.js:2159-2168). Effect: a gate outage does not degrade gracefully, it blocks ~100% of pallet-exchange invoicing fleet-wide (own code comment at invoicing.js:139-141 predicts exactly this, but the fallback data source has since gone dead).
failure_modes.gap: No check alerts on INV.gateFailed itself (a frontend-only flag, never logged to the backend) — the accountant sees a banner in the moment, but nobody downstream (owner, audit) learns a gate outage happened or how many orders it blocked that day.

failure_modes.what: The 'only owner can undo Invoiced' rule (commit 4801db4) is enforced ONLY client-side (`if (ROLE !== 'owner') return`, invoicing.js:902). The Worker's handleFacadeUpdate/invoiceMarkError never checks role for the invoiced:true->false transition, and PERMISSIONS grants accountant and dispatcher plain PATCH on orders/national_orders (all fields). Any accountant or dispatcher session — via a script, an extension, or a future UI bug — can call PATCH /v0/orders {Invoiced:false, 'Invoice Number':null, 'Invoice Date':null} directly and it succeeds silently (no 403, no trigger objection — 043 only guards the transition TO true).
failure_modes.gap: No B-check, no audit-log alert, and no test exercises this path — worker/test/invoice-mark-guard.test.mjs only proves the price/number guard, not a role guard, because there is none to test.

failure_modes.what: Confirming a movement is 3 sequential HTTP calls (sheet upload -> PATCH taken/given/sheet_source -> POST confirm) with no shared DB transaction. If the PATCH succeeds and the confirm call fails (network blip, session expiry, tab close), the movement is left 'pending' but already carries live taken/given quantities and a sheet_source — indistinguishable in the pending list from one nobody has touched yet, except by re-opening it.
failure_modes.gap: B-17 (pl_pending_7d) would eventually surface it after 7 days, but nothing flags a 'half-confirmed' pending row sooner, and nothing distinguishes it from a genuinely untouched pending row in the UI list.

failure_modes.what: Every feeder failure surfaces as an 8-second toast ('καταχώρησε χειροκίνητα') and then is gone forever — the order save/delivery/assignment that triggered it always succeeds regardless (that is the documented intent). If the toast is missed (daily_ops.js and weekly_intl.js call the feeders WITHOUT await, so the toast can appear well after the user has navigated away), the pallet movement for that stop/delivery/partner-assignment is simply never created, with no record anywhere that it was ever supposed to exist.
failure_modes.gap: No check compares 'orders with Pallet Exchange=true and a Loading stop' against 'has any pl_movements row for that stop' at the population level — B-16/B-17 only see movements that DO exist, never movements that should exist but don't.

failure_modes.what: The pallet-sheet gate (pl_v_order_gate.sheets_ok) has ZERO server-side enforcement. invoiceMarkError checks only invoice_number and price>0; migration 043's trigger checks the same two things; PL_PERMS.override is owner-only but override() only writes an audit row and has no coupling to the actual invoice PATCH. Consequently ANY role with orders/national_orders PATCH (owner, management via '*', accountant, dispatcher) can mark a pallet-exchange order Invoiced=true with valid price+number while sheets_ok=false, WITHOUT ever calling /pallets/override — no 422, no audit trail naming who skipped the gate or why. The entire §4.1 gate described in docs/PALLETS_ARCHITECTURE.md is a UI convention, not a database guarantee.
failure_modes.gap: B-16 measures the QUEUE of gate-blocked-and-not-yet-invoiced orders; it does NOT (and cannot, from its own definition) detect an order that got invoiced while gate-blocked, because sheets_ok=false + invoiced=true rows simply drop out of the B-16 WHERE clause (`o.invoiced IS NOT TRUE`). No check anywhere catches this after the fact.

gaps: The ownership brief lists a table `pl_sheets` — it does not exist. Uploaded pallet sheets live in Supabase STORAGE (bucket `pallet-sheets`, via POST/GET /pallets/sheets), referenced from pl_movements.sheet_url/sheet_source. No Postgres table by that name was found (grep of worker/migrations + db/migrations).

modules/pallet_upload.js and modules/orders_intl.js#_checkPalletSheets are both dead code with zero live callers — kept loaded (app.html:152) and documented as a known critical finding in the code's own comment (orders_intl.js:2159-2168), not rediscovered here.

pallet_ledger_suppliers / pallet_ledger_partners are legacy dead tables (0 rows per docs/PALLETS_ARCHITECTURE.md §5.1) but still carry full write grants in PERMISSIONS for management/accountant/dispatcher — dead permissions on dead data, principle 8 (νεκρός κώδικας λέει ψέματα).

No test file exists for the pallet ledger confirm/reverse/override flow (tests/ and worker/test/ both have zero files matching *pallet*) — only invoicing's price/number guard is tested, not the gate itself, not the 3-step confirm race, not the role gate on undo.

The 63-order figure in check B-16 (22/9) differs from a 51-order figure in a readiness doc dated 21/9 per the review's own coordinator note — not reconciled in any file this team read; flagged there as a to-do for 'Παρασκευή', not resolved.

_invOverrideInvoice's two calls (POST /pallets/override, then atPatch Invoiced) are unlinked by any shared id beyond order_rec appearing in both — if a second override is recorded for the same order later (e.g. retried after a failure), there is no way from the audit_log alone to tell which override attempt corresponds to which eventual invoice write, since neither the audit entry nor the orders row stores an override reference id.

cross_deps.why: syncOrderDownstream is team α's cascade orchestrator; its own callers (order save flows outside orders_intl/natl, e.g. Veroia Switch/groupage paths) determine how often and under what conditions the PE-toggle-only feeder call actually fires — team α should confirm the full caller list of syncOrderDownstream itself.

the feeder reads ORDERS.'Total Pallets', which depends on team α's Worker field map for the orders table staying intact (a prior audit, 25/8, found this exact field silently dropped by the facade, producing 0/0 partner pallet movements).

the Trip PnL partner-pallet gate (costs Φ5) is defined in the same migration (007) as our order gate and reads pl_movements PARTNER_PICKUP/DROPOFF confirmed rows — team β should verify who actually calls/reads ct_v_rt_pallet_gate today and whether its PnL gate has the same 'no server-side enforcement' shape as FM-c-05.

plFetch is the shared HTTP client for every /pallets/* call across invoicing.js, pallet_ledger.js and pallet-feed.js itself; a 401 (expired JWT) surfaces only as whatever string the Worker's jsonError put in data.error — team ε owns the auth/session/audit domain and should confirm whether an expired session mid-pallet-confirm is distinguishable from a genuine 401 permission denial anywhere in the UI.

the override audit entry (action:'invoice_override') is the ONLY record of who bypassed the pallet-sheet gate and why; team ε (audit trail) should confirm whether modules/audit_trail.js actually surfaces this action type distinctly to the owner, given FM-c-05 means the override call can also simply be skipped entirely.
